chunks: With this chain of transmission, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Ḥammād, from Ḥarīz, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who is affected by janābah in a cold land and cannot find water, though it may be that the water is frozen. He said: He should perform ghusl according to what is available. He informed him that he had done that and became ill for a month from the cold. He said: He performed ghusl according to what was available, for ghusl is unavoidable. Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام mentioned that he had been compelled to do it while he was ill, so they brought it to him warmed, and he performed ghusl, and he said: Ghusl is unavoidable.

key_terms.الْجَنَابَةُ: the state of major ritual impurity requiring ghusl
key_terms.جَامِدًا: frozen or solidified due to cold
key_terms.يَغْتَسِلُ: he performs ghusl, the ritual bath

ai.seo_question: What should a person in janābah do if the weather is extremely cold and the water is frozen or harmful to use?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling of a person in janābah under severely cold conditions, emphasizing the necessity of ghusl even when hardship is present. It also mentions the practical measure of warming the water, showing the legal importance of ritual purification while dealing with difficult circumstances.
